brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand-level fabric string is 'PU-coated nylon / polyester (welded)'. CONFIRMED for the Shield line (13L/22L/25L): the maker's spec sheet lists 'Nylon' with 'Waterproof IPX4' rating, and all four Shield photos show a glossy, semi-translucent-at-the-seams tarpaulin finish with no visible stitching - consistent with a PU- or TPU-coated nylon that is heat-welded rather than sewn, matching the brand string closely even though the maker's own spec table doesn't spell out 'PU-coated' or 'welded' in so many words. NOT CONFIRMED for the other two products: the Chasm Handlebar Bag 2L's own page lists 'Material: 420D nylon with phthalate-free laminate' - a laminated (not PU-coated) nylon, and the photo shows a flatter, more matte face than the Shield bags with visible stitched seams, not welded ones - a related but distinct construction. The Paramount Hybrid Pannier 26L's page lists simply 'Material: Polyester' with no coating or seam-construction claim at all; its photos show a technical ripstop-look structured-pack fabric with YKK zip closures, nothing like the glossy welded tarpaulin of the Shield line - this product does not match the brand string's 'PU-coated ... welded' half at all, only the bare 'polyester' word. So the blanket fabric string is accurate for 3 of 5 products (the Shield line) and should not be applied to the Chasm or Paramount.
brand_notes.method: All five Thule product pages returned full 'Technical specifications' tables via plain curl - no JS rendering was needed. Every dims_cm figure (inches on the maker page, converted to cm in brands.json) was re-derived from the raw inches and matched brands.json to within rounding on every product; none disagreed. None of the five products publish a dimension RANGE anywhere on the page - each of L/W/H is a single fixed figure - so the unfurled/min-height rule and the render block have nothing to apply to for any Thule product.
brand_notes.rack_dependency: Four of the five products (all three Shield panniers and the Paramount Hybrid Pannier) are rack-mount panniers with rigid mounting hardware and cannot attach to a bare 56cm drop-bar gravel bike, which has no rear rack in this catalogue's base build - all four are marked fits: 'rack_only'. Only the Chasm Handlebar Bag mounts directly to the bar and needs no rack.
brand_notes.rigid_vs_soft: Thule is a hard-goods brand as expected, but the rigidity is concentrated in the MOUNTING HARDWARE, not the bag bodies, for 3 of the 5 products. Shield 13L/22L/25L: the bag body itself is a soft, pliable welded-tarpaulin roll-top (deformable, like an Ortlieb pannier) - only the top rail/hook-clip bracket bonded to the back panel is rigid and must not deform. Chasm 2L: soft fabric bag throughout, with only a possible light stiffener at the base. Paramount 26L: genuinely semi-rigid/structured through the whole body - it holds a crisp box silhouette unsupported in both product photos (does not sag or collapse like the Shield bags would off the bike), consistent with an internal frame/foam-backed hybrid-pannier-to-backpack shell; this one should NOT be run through the soft-bag deform pass at all, or only minimally.

mount.notes: The second photo shows the actual hardware: a rigid black plastic rail bonded across the top-back of the bag with two spring-loaded hook clips that snap onto a pannier rack rail, plus a rotating knob-adjustable stabilizer foot lower down that presses against the rack leg. This rail/clip assembly is RIGID and must not be run through the soft-bag deform pass, even though the bag body it's bonded to is soft. Requires a rear pannier rack, which the base gravel-bike build in this catalogue does not include - see fits.
